comparison: Both evaluations address the identification of PP2A-B55 as the anti-Endos phosphatase (C3, C24-C36). OpenEval rates this as SUPPORTED with detailed praise for converging evidence from genetic, biochemical, and reconstitution approaches. Peer reviewers also rate this as SUPPORTED, accepting the core finding without challenge and describing it as 'interesting.'

Both address kinetic measurements (C4-C8). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging technical challenges but finding the dramatic differences sufficient for conclusions. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising methodological concerns about appropriateness of Michaelis-Menten kinetics for strongly-bound complexes and lack of variation estimates in data presentation.

OpenEval R3 addresses differential M phase vs interphase activity (C9-C11) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 addresses overlapping pharmacological claims (C9-C11 plus C12-C23, C37) but rates as UNCERTAIN due to unclear assay descriptions and inconsistencies in inhibitor sensitivities. Partial overlap with different evaluation outcomes.

OpenEval R4 addresses comprehensive pharmacological characterization (C12-C23) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes these claims (C12-C23, C37) along with C9-C11 but rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning assay methodology, linearity with enzyme concentration, and inconsistencies between experiments.

Both address competitive inhibition mechanism (C38-C44, C85). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with praise for multiple lines of evidence demonstrating active site competition. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, finding the model 'very beautiful' conceptually but questioning whether experimental validation adequately demonstrates rate independence from complex dilution.

Both address concentration estimates and stoichiometry (C45-C49, C86). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding Western blot quantitation consistent with mass spec data and supporting the model. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting measurement of pEndos to PP2A-B55 ratios as critical validation for the proposed mechanism.

Both address mathematical modeling (C51-C54). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding models appropriately based on experimental parameters and effectively demonstrating necessity of unfair competition. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the mechanism is rapid enough for mitotic exit and whether measurements in asynchronous cells are physiologically relevant.

Both address Gwl-inactivating phosphatase identity (C55-C58). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting sound logic but preliminary/incomplete experimental evidence. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concerns about circular logic: Gwl inactivation may require active PP2A-B55, yet the model assumes Gwl inactivation precedes PP2A-B55 reactivation.

Both address exclusion of Fcp1 (C59-C63). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with multiple independent lines of evidence. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting this negative result without challenge as supporting PP2A-B55 identification.

Both address established background knowledge and regulatory circuit context (C1, C2, C66-C78). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting these are well-established claims from literature. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the conceptual framework without challenge.

OpenEval R11 addresses PP2A structure and Drosophila genetics background (C79-C84). Peer R9 includes some overlapping background claims (C79-C84 within broader C1-C91 set). Both rate as SUPPORTED for established background information.

Both address the unfair competition model synthesis (C50, C87-C91). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing this as the major conceptual advance integrating multiple evidence lines. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED for the conceptual framework, describing it as 'very beautiful' with intrinsic reset mechanism, though they questioned specific mechanistic details elsewhere.

Minor overlap on C87 (unfair competition model). OpenEval R12 addresses the complete model synthesis as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 focuses on stoichiometry requirements (C45-C49, C86-C87) and rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting validation that pEndos exceeds PP2A-B55.

Both address the PP1/Inhibitor-1 parallel (C64-C65). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citation providing historical context. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting this as established precedent without challenge.
